tier2_explanatory.long_meaning: From the Hebrew Miriam. Standard interpretations give 'beloved' or 'rebellious'; a popular alternative links it to mara, 'bitter'. Its root is Hebrew m-r-y-m. Miriam, sister of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 15:20). Miriam is a Hebrew name meaning “Beloved; (also) bitter; rebellious”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
